Visit us at www.gcggroup.com GCG is seeking a Food Safety & Quality Specialist who will play a vital role in providing technical leadership for food safety and quality programs, supporting operational teams in the identification, prevention, and mitigation of food safety and quality risks while ensuring compliance with regulatory, customer, and corporate requirements. JOB PURPOSE The Food Safety & Quality Specialist is accountable for the technical adequacy of the Group’s food safety and quality standards and the effectiveness of related controls across stations. The role translates applicable requirements into practical programs, directs technical implementation, and verifies that controls protect food safety and meet product and service specifications. The position requires timely correction of deficiencies, validates technical solutions, and escalates unresolved risks. It develops local capabilities and supervises the Food Safety & Quality Coordinator, while Operations retains responsibility for daily execution and sustained implementation of controls. Duties & Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Technical Requirements & Standards · Establish and maintain food safety and quality requirements within the approved corporate framework. · Translate applicable regulatory, corporate, and customer requirements into operational standards and technical controls. · Assess proposed local adaptations and approve them within delegated authority or submit them to the QHSE Lead for approval. · Require correction of practices that do not meet approved requirements and escalate unresolved technical disagreements. · Obtain additional technical expertise when a requirement or proposed solution exceeds the available competence. Food Safety & Quality Programs · Define and maintain the technical requirements for HACCP, prerequisite programs, hygiene controls, allergen management, traceability, and food safety verification. · Review station food safety plans and support evidence to confirm that hazards and controls reflect actual products, processes, and operating conditions. · Establish validation and verification priorities, including microbiological testing and shelf-life studies, and evaluate the adequacy of methods and results. · Define quality control criteria with relevant process owners to verify compliance with approved product and service specifications. · Supervise the Food Safety & Quality Coordinator’s technical work, review deliverables, and require correction of incomplete or unreliable evidence. · Verify that program results lead to appropriate action when controls or product performance fall below requirements. Cross-Disciplinary Coordination · Coordinate with the HSSE Specialist where occupational safety, ramp activities, physical security, or environmental controls may affect food safety or quality. · Review cross-disciplinary risks associated with facilities, maintenance, equipment, chemicals, loading, and transport. · Define food safety and quality requirements for shared interventions without assuming technical ownership of other disciplines. · Escalate conflicting requirements to the QHSE Lead and contribute to technically sound, practical resolutions. Local Technical Direction · Provide functional technical direction to designated local food safety and quality representatives. · Require implementation of approved standards, completion of assigned technical programs, and timely submission of reliable evidence. · Review local performance and challenge inadequate controls, unsupported conclusions, or ineffective corrective responses. · Coordinate resource and implementation requirements with station management and local OPEX Managers, where present. · Provide technical performance feedback and escalate capability or execution gaps without replacing local personnel management responsibilities. Technical Visits & Inspections · Conduct food safety and quality inspections according to the corporate intervention plan and emerging risks. · Evaluate actual operating practices and control effectiveness through observation, records, interviews, and relevant technical results. · Document deficiencies, communicate required corrective outcomes, and establish response deadlines within delegated authority. · Require follow-up verification or reassessment when submitted evidence is insufficient or failures recur. · Approve closure of technical inspection deficiencies within delegated authority, based on demonstrated implementation and effectiveness. · Provide technical validation to EA for deficiencies linked to corporate audit findings; EA retains the formal closure decision . Incidents, Deviations & Corrective Actions · Require immediate containment of significant food safety or quality risks in accordance with applicable procedures and delegated authority. · Lead the technical evaluation of significant incidents, complaints, and recurring deviations, coordinating investigations with process owners. · Challenge root cause analyses that lack evidence or fail to explain the identified control failure. · Approve or reject the technical adequacy of corrective action plans within delegated authority and require revision of insufficient solutions. · Verify implementation and sustained effectiveness, escalating overdue actions, continuing exposure, or recurring failures. · Provide technical recommendations on affected products or processes; disposition, suspension, and restart decisions follow the applicable authorization requirements. · Inform EA when new evidence indicates that a previously closed corporate audit finding may require reassessment. Visit us at www.gcggroup.com GCG is seeking a Health, Safety, Security & Environment (HSSE) Specialist who will play a vital role in establishing, implementing, and monitoring HSSE programs and controls across our airport and operational locations, ensuring compliance, risk reduction, and a safe working environment for team members, customers, and stakeholders. JOB PURPOSE The HSSE Specialist is accountable for the technical adequacy of the Group’s health, safety, security, and operational environmental requirements and the effectiveness of related controls across stations, including ramp operations. The role establishes preventive controls, directs technical implementation, investigates significant deviations, and requires timely corrective action. It develops local capabilities, verifies control effectiveness, and escalates unresolved risks, while Operations retains responsibility for daily execution and sustained implementation of controls. Duties & Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Technical Requirements & Standards Establish and maintain HSSE requirements within the approved corporate framework. Translate applicable regulatory, airport, corporate, and customer requirements, together with relevant international standards and guidance, into practical operational controls. Assess proposed local adaptations and approve them within delegated authority or submit them to the QHSE Lead for approval. Require correction of practices that do not meet approved requirements and escalate unresolved technical disagreements. Obtain additional expertise when a requirement, assessment, or proposed solution exceeds the available technical competence. Health, Safety, Security & Environment Programs Establish and maintain programs for occupational hazard identification, risk assessment, injury prevention, and emergency preparedness. Define and verify ramp safety requirements for activities around aircraft, including equipment positioning, vehicle movements, loading, unloading, and coordination between operational teams. Establish physical security controls within the department’s scope, including access control, protection of facilities and products, and reporting of security concerns. Define operational environmental controls for waste, chemicals, spills, and other applicable impacts. Review station programs and supporting evidence to confirm that controls reflect actual activities, equipment, facilities, and operating conditions. Coordinate specialized assessments or services where occupational health, security, or environmental matters require additional professional expertise. Cross-Disciplinary Coordination Coordinate with the Food Safety & Quality Specialist where HSSE controls may affect hygiene, food safety, product protection, or service quality. Review shared risks associated with maintenance, cleaning chemicals, facilities, loading, transport, and emergency response. Define HSSE requirements for shared interventions without assuming technical ownership of food safety and quality. Coordinate with Operations, Maintenance, HR, and other responsible functions on corrective measures that require changes to equipment, facilities, work practices, or personnel arrangements. Escalate conflicting requirements to the QHSE Lead and contribute to practical, technically sound resolutions. Risk Prevention & Performance Analysis Apply approved criteria to identify hazards, assess risks, and prioritize preventive or corrective interventions. Evaluate station performance using inspections, incident reports, near misses, control verification, and other relevant evidence. Identify recurring failures, overdue actions, and gaps in the effectiveness of preventive controls. Establish technical remediation priorities and deadlines proportionate to risk, within approved procedures. Require targeted corrective responses and report material risks or unresolved deficiencies to the QHSE Lead and relevant operational leadership. Promote accurate reporting of incidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions to support prevention and learning. Local Technical Direction Provide functional technical direction to designated local representatives responsible for occupational safety, ramp safety, physical security, and environmental controls. Require implementation of approved requirements, completion of assigned programs, and timely submission of reliable evidence. Challenge inadequate controls, unsupported conclusions, or ineffective corrective responses. Coordinate resource and implementation requirements with station management and local OPEX Managers, where present. Provide technical performance feedback and escalate capability or execution gaps without replacing local personnel management responsibilities. Technical Visits & Inspections Conduct HSSE inspections according to the corporate intervention plan and emerging operational risks. Evaluate work practices and control effectiveness through observation, records, interviews, and relevant technical assessments. Document deficiencies, communicate required corrective outcomes, and establish response deadlines within delegated authority. review_candidates.description: Reporting to the Managing Director, Head of Latin America, the Channel Marketing Manager will translate established business and marketing priorities into integrated campaigns, advertising, content, digital experiences, sales enablement and partner initiatives. The role will collaborate with Distribution, Product Management, Digital, Marketing Operations, Compliance and external partners to deliver coordinated, effective and locally relevant marketing programs across Latin America. Essential Duties And Responsibilities Includes the following, other duties may be assigned as needed: Execute integrated marketing initiatives that support business priorities, distribution objectives and focus products across Latin America. Support select U.S. Offshore marketing initiatives as directed and where aligned with broader business priorities. Develop high-quality campaigns and content supporting priority investment strategies, market opportunities and Distribution objectives. Partner with digital and creative agencies to develop campaign concepts, advertising copy and creative assets for Latin American audiences. Manage the end-to-end creative development process, including briefs, stakeholder feedback, revisions, Compliance review and final production. Adapt and leverage existing U.S., European and global campaigns and content for Latin American audiences, ensuring regional relevance and appropriate localization. Develop and coordinate marketing programs across paid media, email, websites, third-party platforms, content distribution and sales enablement channels. Work with publishers, media partners and distribution platforms to promote VanEck research, investment commentary, videos and product content. Partner with the LATAM Marketing Operations & Content Strategist to maintain and optimize VanEck’s Latin America websites and support select updates to U.S. Offshore digital properties as needed. Collaborate on SEO and AEO initiatives to improve organic visibility, content discoverability and engagement across VanEck’s Latin America digital properties. Review Spanish-language marketing materials and translations to ensure they are accurate, natural and appropriate for Latin American audiences. Coordinate Portuguese-language adaptations as needed. Partner with the Managing Director, Head of Latin America and Distribution teams to understand sales needs, client opportunities and upcoming business priorities. Develop and maintain sales enablement materials, including presentations, product messaging, emails, campaign materials and other resources. Support conferences, roadshows, due diligence meetings, webinars, client events and educational programs, including related marketing materials and communications. Develop and coordinate marketing support for product launches, cross-listings and other strategic regional initiatives. Partner with Product Management to ensure investment strategies and focus products are positioned accurately, consistently and effectively. Collaborate with Compliance throughout the review and approval process for marketing materials. Track and analyze campaign, websites, advertising and content performance, using results to identify optimization opportunities and inform future initiatives. Coordinate with internal Creative, Digital, Marketing Operations, Events, Data and other Marketing teams to ensure the timely execution of regional priorities. Manage relationships and workflows with agencies, publishers, translators, consultants and other external partners as needed. Help develop scalable processes that improve the efficiency, consistency and quality of marketing execution across Latin America. Qualifications Strong understanding of integrated and digital marketing, including paid media, email, websites, content distribution and third-party platforms. Experience working with creative or digital agencies to develop and execute advertising and marketing campaigns. Superior written and interpersonal communication skills, with strong attention to detail and quality assurance. Excellent project management and proven delivery skills. Ability to analyze marketing performance and KPIs and use results to optimize campaigns and marketing programs. Demonstrated success integrating marketing initiatives across channels in support of common business goals and objectives. Ability to work in a deadline-driven environment with changing priorities; self-sufficient, proactive and well-organized. Excellent Spanish-language writing and editing skills, including the ability to review and adapt marketing content for Latin American audiences. Experience collaborating effectively with senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams across Latin America, the U.S. and Europe, including in a distributed working environment. Familiarity with SEO, AEO and evolving digital content discovery practices preferred. Experience with CMS platforms and digital analytics and project management tools preferred. Experience working with ETFs, asset management or financial services products preferred; familiarity with investment products and financial markets is a plus. Experience supporting Latin American audiences preferred; experience supporting U.S. Offshore audiences is a plus. Strong understanding of regional language, cultural and market nuances across Latin America preferred. Ability to travel periodically within Latin America and to the U.S. to support client events, conferences and other business initiatives as needed. Education And/or Experience 5–7 years of relevant marketing experience. Bachelor's degree preferably in marketing, business, communications, finance or economics. Professional fluency in English and Spanish required. Experience supporting Latin American and/or US Offshore audiences preferred. Background in bilingual content localization and translation coordination preferred. Portuguese language skills or experience supporting the Brazilian market are a plus.
